text:
No option can be put forward yet, because the model could not assess your “monthly churn < 4%” limit.

- The comparison was robust under the changes tested, but that does not establish compliance with the churn limit; the model measures churn as a calculated change rather than a monthly churn rate on the same scale.
- The goal direction was not stated, so the comparison assumed that more MRR is better. The £20k/month threshold also could not be checked against the model’s output frame.
- The most sensitive model input is the Pro subscriber base—an Olumi estimate, not user evidence. The price-to-MRR link was fragile under its own perturbation test; that is not an overall stability measure.

The current finding is therefore incomplete rather than a basis for a pricing decision.
